Keywords: Horn sinew bow glue and damp
RagShortTexts: Wood, horn, sinew and glue share the load in a composite bow.
Damp and damaged glue layers impair the bow.

Variants.Content: A horn-and-sinew composite bow combines materials whose glue joints and coverings need care. Archers inspect strings and joins and avoid prolonged damp or careless heating. A damaged bow requires skilled repair, not simply a replacement string.
On wet marches an archer protects the bow and spare strings, then checks joins. Pulling through unusual noises or separation may destroy a repairable bow; pursuit cannot replace maintenance.
Supporting archers requires string material, suitable arrows and skilled repairers. Money cannot instantly replace damage; weather and repair locations limit the number of usable bows on campaign.
Bow materials need joining, shaping and time to set. Rushed work wastes horn, sinew and glue; buyers denying drying and adjustment time bear breakage and replacement costs.
